sources.entry: Terminator - Terminal emulator that lets you open multiple GNOME terminals in one window.

summary.one_liner: Terminator is a GNOME-oriented terminal emulator that lets you split one window into multiple terminals and group them to control several at once.
summary.what_it_does: Terminator opens a terminal in a window with a titlebar that updates as shells or programs set it. Terminals can be split horizontally and vertically inside one window, and organized into tabs. A grouping menu on the titlebar lets you put terminals into groups so you can control several simultaneously. The README lists default keyboard shortcuts for splitting, moving focus, opening tabs and windows, closing, and resetting zoom, and says these are modifiable under Preferences > Keybindings. Documentation is available as man pages (terminator and terminator_config) and on the web via F1. The README says it was originally inspired by quadkonsole, gnome-multi-term, iTerm2, and Tilix.
use_cases: Running multiple shells side by side in one window
Controlling several remote machines at once
Splitting a terminal window horizontally or vertically
Organizing terminals into tabs and groups
how_to_run: Install from your Linux distribution's package repository (search for 'terminator'); also available on FreeBSD
For building from source or the master branch, see INSTALL.md (referenced in the README)
Open a new tab: Ctrl-Shift-t; new window: Ctrl-Shift-i
See man terminator and man terminator_config for more
stack: VTE terminal widget (referenced in README origins)
notable: Split and recombine terminals within one window, with horizontal and vertical splits
Terminal grouping menu on the titlebar to broadcast control to multiple terminals
Keyboard shortcuts are fully modifiable via Preferences
Originally a roughly 300-line Python script from 2007, now maintained by a new team since 2020
Packaged in most Linux distributions and FreeBSD
caveats: Installation is primarily through distribution packages; building from source needs the INSTALL.md steps
New issues go to the GitHub project; the older Launchpad project should not receive new posts
